chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Mukhtar, from Al-A'ala ibn Kamil, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When you mingle with the people, if you have the capacity to not mingle with anyone from the people except that your hand would be higher upon him, then do so. For indeed, the servant may have some deficiency in worship, but he has good manners, so Allah will bring him, due to his good manners, to the rank of the fasting one who stands (in prayer).'

key_terms.الصَّائِمِ الْقَائِمِ: the fasting one who stands (in prayer)
key_terms.خَالَطْتَ: to mingle or mix with people

ai.seo_question: How can good manners compensate for deficiencies in ritual worship according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the compensatory power of *husn al-khuluq* (excellent character), noting that it can elevate a believer to the rank of the *Saim al-Qaim* (one who fasts and prays extensively) despite deficiencies in ritual worship. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on social ethics as a vital component of spiritual perfection, where moral conduct serves as a means of grace (*fadl*) that bridges the gap between imperfect practice and divine acceptance.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Al Husayn Bin Al Mukhtar, from Al A’ala Bin Kamil who said,

‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘When you mingle with the people, so if you have the capacity that you would not mingle with anyone from the people except that your hand would be higher upon his, then do so. So if the servant happens to have in him part of the deficiency from the worship, and there happens to be good manners for him, then Allahazwj would Make him to reach, due to his good manners, the level of the Fasting one, the standing one (for Salāt)’.
en.sarwar: 14. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from al- Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar from ‘Ala’ ibn Kamil

from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “In your association with people you should have the upper hand (to benefit them), if you are able to do so. A servant (of Allah) who has shortcomings in his worship may have commendable moral behavior with which Allah grants him a reward of the degree of one who worships all nights and fasts all days.”
